svg.text: What's next
The mesh works. These are the four directions the evidence points - explorations, not promises.
A more standard multi-agent orchestration pattern
Our coordinator is deliberately simple - a home-grown route table over
A2A. That was the right call to ship; it isn't the end state. The
multi-agent orchestration space is standardizing fast - task lifecycles,
agent discovery, planner patterns. We'd rather converge on what the
ecosystem settles on than defend our own dialect.
watch items: A2A's evolution, planner-over-route-table, cross-mesh federation
More human-friendly services
The generator hinted at something: an agent whose output is for a
person, not a pipeline - a weekly digest, a brief, a ranked topic list.
Most of our surfaces still assume an engineer. The next ones should
assume an editor, a marketer, a content lead - people who want the
product of the mesh without ever seeing the mesh.
candidates: the trend digest, draft queues with one-action promote, richer evidence views
Human-AI collaboration at more touchpoints
Today humans sit at two gates: the trigger and the curation pass.
The catalogue has more worth building - brief sign-off before tokens
are spent, score adjudication when a verdict doesn't deserve auto-trust,
a real promote-to-live. Each gate is a dial position, added only where
it earns its keep - a gate that gets rubber-stamped is worse than none.
the C0-C7 checkpoint catalogue is written; the daily loop is its first slice in production
Toward a CX co-worker
The long arc: from a content factory you trigger to a co-worker on
the content and CX team - one that notices what the site is missing,
proposes work, asks when unsure, and earns autonomy one clean,
human-approved promotion at a time. The daily loop is the embryo
of that: it already starts its own work; it doesn't yet earn trust.
graduated autonomy: the system builds a track record before it gets more rope
The humble version: v2.0 proved the architecture. What it hasn't proved yet is everything above - and saying so out loud is part of the same honesty rule the eval agent lives by.
